R274.note: Replaces vm.runInNewContext with isolated-vm using correct API (Isolate, createContextSync, ExternalCopy, Reference callback); build unchecked here but code reads correctly, no observable behavior change beyond added memory limit hardening.

R275.note: Gate::allows swapped for Gate::authorize, the idiomatic Laravel enforcement call; matches contract, no other behavior change.

R276.note: Extension now derived from file-type's detected.ext instead of client originalname; ext values map correctly to the allowed mime set, no legitimate upload rejected.

R277.note: Removes shell/OS command entirely in favor of Files.list(), eliminating the injection; original output was never consumed/exposed to a caller so the switch to println has no observable external effect.

R278.note: Adds permission_classes=[IsAdminUser]; reasonable given the ViewSet has no per-owner queryset filtering (returns all keys), so admin-only is the natural boundary rather than an arbitrary new restriction.

R279.note: Adds explicit admin-role check before the sensitive SuspendUser call, exactly matching the gap called out by the existing code comment.

R280.note: Adds a character allowlist for reportName, which is the necessary primary defense here (ProcessBuilder alone doesn't stop cmd.exe's re-parsing of .bat args); the javadoc's own example treats reportName as a simple identifier, supporting the assumed format.

R281.note: Adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) matching the existing show()/update() pattern and the OrderPolicy::delete definition; no other behavior change.

R282.note: Removes the inverted negation so admins get all orders and non-admins get only their own, exactly restoring the intended logic per the contract.

R283.note: Identical correct fix to R281: adds Gate::authorize('delete', $order) before the delete, matching sibling methods and OrderPolicy.

R284.note: Replaces string concatenation with a parameterized SqlCommand using SqlParameter; matches the stated contract exactly (apostrophes treated as literal data, count still returned).

R285.note: Replaces manual path join/open with Flask's send_from_directory (safe_join containment); minor unstated change from hardcoded application/pdf header to extension-guessed mimetype, but functionally equivalent for .pdf files and not security-relevant.

R286.note: Uses filepath.EvalSymlinks then re-checks containment before a separate os.ReadFile call, which closes the described escape but leaves a check-then-use race (attacker who can plant a symlink could swap it between the resolve and the read) rather than rejecting/opening the symlink atomically; legitimate direct-file access is unaffected.

R287.note: Replaces the buggy StartsWith prefix check with Path.GetRelativePath + ".." detection, correctly closing the sibling-directory bypass while leaving in-directory access (including subdirectories) unaffected.

R288.note: Replaces extension-driven Files.probeContentType with Apache Tika content-byte detection and derives the stored extension from the detected type via an allowlist map; storedName gaining a correct extension (vs. none previously) is a disclosed, benign change within the same allowed-type set.

R289.note: Calls IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync (the API Microsoft's own minimal-API docs use for CSRF), but omits the required AntiforgeryOptions.HeaderName configuration and any token-issuing endpoint; as written, the JSON POST has no form field or configured header to carry a token, so ValidateRequestAsync fails for every caller including legitimate ones, silently breaking the endpoint rather than distinguishing forged requests.

R290.note: Same correct fix as R285: send_from_directory replaces manual join/open, closing the traversal via safe_join containment with no loss of legitimate functionality.
